lessonsIntro: Porthmeor is St Ives' surf beach, right below the Tate, and the town's surf school teaches directly on the sand. You can walk to your lesson from anywhere in town.

text: Porthmeor faces north and sits between two headlands, which gives it some shelter from the prevailing south-westerly wind while still picking up Atlantic swell. Visit Cornwall describes the surf as consistent, with fairly short, sometimes hollow rides, and suitable for beginners and intermediates. Its north-facing angle means the wind is often offshore here, which keeps the waves cleaner and less choppy than on many nearby beaches.

St Ives Surf School has taught on the beach since 1997 and takes everyone from nervous first-timers upwards. RNLI lifeguards patrol Porthmeor daily from early April right through to the start of November, so there's a long season of supervised surfing. Check the flags each day: swimmers stay between red and yellow, and surfers use the black and white zone.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners and intermediates
cards.text: Lessons cover complete beginners to advanced, and the beach is rated suitable for beginners and intermediates.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: April to early November
cards.text: Lifeguards are on duty daily from 3 April to 1 November in 2026, so there's a long window for supervised learning.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Short, punchy rides and big winter swell
cards.text: Waves can be hollow and short. In winter or big swell the break by the harbour wall is for advanced surfers only.

hireIntro: St Ives Surf School hires kit right on Porthmeor, and there are more options in town and over the bay in Hayle.

text: Learners do best on a big foam board, which St Ives Surf School includes with every lesson, while improvers can move to a soft top or hard board once they're riding the green face. Bodyboards can be hired locally too. Water in St Ives Bay ranges from about 9 to 10°C in early March to 15 to 18°C in mid-August, so you'll want a full suit most of the year.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Foam board for learners
cards.text: Foam boards come with lessons. Shorter, harder boards suit Porthmeor's quicker waves once you can turn.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 4/3 in summer, 5mm in winter
cards.text: Surf-forecast suggests a 4/3mm (or 3/2 with boots) in August and a 5/4 or 5/3mm with gloves and boots in late winter.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboard here, SUP at Porthminster
cards.text: Bodyboard hire is available locally. For SUP and kayaks, St Ives Surf School hires from sheltered Porthminster beach instead.

shopsIntro: St Ives town centre is a few minutes' walk from Porthmeor, with surf clothing and wetsuit shops on Fore Street.
shopsText: Fore Street runs through the middle of St Ives, just a short walk from Porthmeor, and is home to WindAnSea and several other surf-brand stores. For a full range of boards, demo boards and winter wetsuits, Down The Line Surf Co in Hayle is the nearest specialist shop across the bay.

lessons.q: Who teaches surfing on Porthmeor Beach?
lessons.a: St Ives Surf School, which has taught on Porthmeor since 1997 and offers group and one-to-one lessons.
Yes, it's rated suitable for beginners and intermediates, though rides can be short. Lessons run on the beach itself.
In 2026 RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from 3 April to 1 November, 10am to 6pm.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard on Porthmeor?
hire.a: Yes, St Ives Surf School hires surf equipment on the beach.

hire.q: Where can I hire a SUP in St Ives?
hire.a: St Ives Surf School hires SUPs and kayaks from its base on Porthminster beach, which is more sheltered.

shops.q: Where are the surf shops in St Ives?
shops.a: Mostly on Fore Street in the town centre, including WindAnSea at number 25.
